nodes.label: Strategic Structure
nodes.description: The primary unit of explanation: an enduring arrangement that organizes relationships among actors and resources, constrains and enables particular possibilities, persists across time, and generates recurring outcome patterns. Formally defined within Go-Shape Theory; exhibits both structural properties (persistence, stability, brittleness, resilience, flexibility, transparency) and structural functions (constraining, coordinating, maintaining consistency, enabling adaptation, communicating credibility, allocating resources).

nodes.label: Deep Structure
nodes.description: The underlying, stable foundations of a system, such as Tier 1 values, identity, and core purpose.

nodes.label: Surface Structure
nodes.description: Observable implementations like business models, policies, technical code, and buildings.

nodes.label: Enduring Intent
nodes.description: A deeply held, enduring organizing purpose that persists across specific decisions and translates deep structure into surface behavior. It is contained within deep structure and generates surface structure -- the generative link between the two.

nodes.label: The Sovereign Constitution
nodes.description: The 'dogmatic' internal layer defining why and should via principles that remain constant despite context.

nodes.label: The Engagement Playbook
nodes.description: The 'pragmatic' external layer defining how and what via adaptive tactics.

nodes.label: Clarity
nodes.description: The system discipline of removing distortion between perception and reality.

nodes.label: Method Marks
nodes.description: A non-binary evaluation system for decision quality based on process rather than luck.

nodes.label: The Sovereign Shell
nodes.description: A model-agnostic governance layer for Agentic AI enforcing constitutional determinism.

nodes.label: Constitutional Hiring
nodes.description: A competency-based recruitment architecture built on transparency and demonstrated capability.

nodes.label: Project Collapse
nodes.description: A behavioral ontology and audit system for conversational risk assessment (scam intelligence).

nodes.label: S1: Virtue (The North Star)
nodes.description: Non-negotiable core values and purpose.

nodes.label: S2: Integrity (The Meta-Rule)
nodes.description: Alignment of behavior with core; prohibits deception.

nodes.label: S3: Right Process
nodes.description: Fairness, transparency, and reciprocity in method.

nodes.label: S4: Most Acceptable Outcome
nodes.description: Optimizing for legitimacy and multi-stakeholder sustainability.

nodes.label: S5: Just Cause (师出有名)
nodes.description: Publicly defensible reasoning for every action.

nodes.label: S6: Consistency as Proof
nodes.description: Longitudinal coherence validated by time.

nodes.label: S7: Responsibility of Design
nodes.description: Accountability for foreseeable consequences of created systems.

nodes.label: The Method-Mark Triad
nodes.description: Composed of Signal (actual actions), Noise (external luck/timing), and Calibration (updated competence model).

nodes.label: The Intent Audit Protocol
nodes.description: Composed of Surface Intent, Beneficiary Analysis, Hidden Intent (Five Whys), and Falsification Criteria.

nodes.label: Guru vs. Architect Diagnostic
nodes.description: Evaluates if a framework is Transparent, Falsifiable, Independent, and Transferable.

nodes.label: The M.I.R.R.O.R.
nodes.description: Activities including Modeling self-correction, Integrity under pressure, Rebuilding from criticism, Refusing premature yesses, Opening communication, and Recording the work.

nodes.label: Sovereign Shell Protocol
nodes.description: Sequential phases of Classify, Verify, Bound, Log, and Escalate.

nodes.label: Constitutional Hiring Gates
nodes.description: Includes Standardized Assessment, Anonymous Debrief, and Contextual Resume Review.

nodes.label: Persistence
nodes.description: Degree of change over time.

nodes.label: Stability
nodes.description: Resistance to internal disruption.

nodes.label: Brittleness
nodes.description: Susceptibility to sudden failure under stress.

nodes.label: Resilience
nodes.description: Capacity to recover after disruption.

nodes.label: Flexibility
nodes.description: Capacity to accommodate change without losing coherence.

nodes.label: Transparency
nodes.description: Legibility of the structure to its actors.

nodes.label: Alignment
nodes.description: The degree of match between deep and surface structures.

nodes.label: Go-Shape Theory
nodes.description: A conceptual framework treating structure as the primary unit of theoretical explanation: design determines possibility before action determines outcome.

nodes.label: Structural Properties
nodes.description: Characteristics of a structure itself: persistence, stability, brittleness, resilience, flexibility, compatibility, transparency, efficiency.

nodes.label: Structural Functions
nodes.description: What a structure does: constraining, coordinating, maintaining consistency, enabling adaptation, communicating credibility, allocating resources.

nodes.label: Structural Interaction
nodes.description: How multiple structures operate simultaneously: reinforcement, conflict, dominance, emergence, adaptation.

nodes.label: Proposition 1: Outcomes Require Structure
nodes.description: Enduring strategic outcomes require a sustaining structure; outcomes generated by action alone will tend to dissipate.

nodes.label: Proposition 2: Structures Constrain Actions
nodes.description: Structures constrain the range of strategically available actions prior to any specific decision.

nodes.label: Proposition 3: Aligned Structures Persist
nodes.description: Surface structures from aligned deep structures exhibit greater persistence than those imposed without alignment.

nodes.label: Proposition 4: Alignment Predicts Effectiveness
nodes.description: Degree of alignment between deep and surface structures is positively associated with effectiveness.

nodes.label: Proposition 5: Misalignment Generates Friction
nodes.description: Structural misalignment generates observable friction: inconsistency, resistance, or reversion.

nodes.label: Proposition 6: Identical Surfaces Diverge by Intent
nodes.description: Behaviorally identical surface structures diverge in long-run persistence when enduring intent differs.

nodes.label: Structural Dynamics
nodes.description: How structures change, strengthen, or decay over time (future research direction).

nodes.label: Influence Mechanisms
nodes.description: How structures propagate effects across actors and levels (future research direction).

nodes.label: Cross-Domain Application
nodes.description: Extending the framework to business strategy, government policy, AI governance, and individual decision-making.

nodes.label: Positioning Theory (Porter)
nodes.description: Existing strategy perspective: explains how firms exploit industry structure.

nodes.label: Resource-Based View (Barney)
nodes.description: Existing strategy perspective: explains how firms exploit resource endowments.

nodes.label: Dynamic Capabilities (Teece)
nodes.description: Existing strategy perspective: explains how firms reconfigure resources over time.

nodes.label: Institutional Theory (DiMaggio & Powell)
nodes.description: Existing strategy perspective: explains how firms respond to legitimacy pressures.

nodes.label: Structuration Theory (Giddens)
nodes.description: Social theory treating structure and agency as mutually constituting; Go-Shape narrows scope to strategic structures.

nodes.label: Stable / Adaptive Duality
nodes.description: A universal pattern across all enduring systems: stable foundations (identity, principles, intent, purpose) generate adaptive execution (methods, policies, learning, behaviour). Examples: DNA↔Gene expression, Constitution↔Legislation, Mission↔Strategy, Architecture↔Features, AI Constitution↔LLM reasoning.

nodes.label: Source of Inspiration
nodes.description: Where ideas originate: Daoism, Buddhism, business experience, conversations, systems thinking. Generates hypotheses but does not validate them. Distinct from and prior to Source of Justification.

nodes.label: Source of Justification
nodes.description: The epistemic filter that validates hypotheses: evidence, logical consistency, operationalization, falsification, predictive power. Determines whether a hypothesis stands or falls.

nodes.label: Kalama Sutta
nodes.description: An epistemological anchor from Buddhist canon: do not believe because of authority; do not reject because of authority; observe, test, evaluate consequences, and decide for yourself. Inspires the research methodology.

nodes.label: Continuous Calibration
nodes.description: The philosophy that perfection is not a destination but a state of continuous calibration. Applies to constitutions, organizations, scientific theories, AI, and personal development. Stage 1: near perfection; Stage 2: nothing is perfect; Stage 3: perfect is continuous calibration.

nodes.label: Research Philosophy
nodes.description: Reality precedes strategy. Strategize for the reality that exists, not the illusion we prefer. Dreams are valuable, but strategy begins with accurately perceiving constraints. The question is not whether constraints exist, but whether they should be accepted, worked around, or deliberately broken.

nodes.label: Inspiration-Justification Boundary
nodes.description: The strict separation between where ideas come from (religious, philosophical, experiential traditions) and how claims are validated (scientific criteria). Religious traditions become sources of inspiration; hypotheses then stand or fall according to scientific criteria.

nodes.label: Constitutional Governance
nodes.description: The shift from 'How do we build trustworthy AI?' to 'How do we build constitutional governance around AI?' The LLM becomes one governed actor among many; the constitution governs reasoning, transparency, evidence, responsibility, and amendment.

nodes.label: Observation Log
nodes.description: The bridge between reality and theory. Purpose: reduce subjective interpretation, standardize observations, collect evidence, and support future falsification. Not merely data collection but the disciplined observation layer of the research programme.

nodes.label: Falsification Criteria
nodes.description: For every proposition in the graph: what evidence would cause this proposition to be revised? Each proposition should ideally contain supporting evidence, confidence level, known exceptions, and revision conditions. Prevents belief preservation.

nodes.label: Methodology Cycle
nodes.description: The iterative research process: Observe → Hypothesis → Operationalize → Collect Evidence → Refine Theory → Repeat. Inspired by the Kalama Sutta and aligned with scientific method.

nodes.label: Constitutional Reasoning Engine
nodes.description: The knowledge graph's function: not merely stored knowledge, but explainable AI. Each node may eventually contain definition, evidence, supporting propositions, confidence, competing explanations, amendment history, and reasoning links.

nodes.label: Amendment
nodes.description: The capacity of a constitutional structure to revise itself. A core function of the Sovereign Constitution, the Knowledge Graph, and the Constitutional Reasoning Engine. Without amendment, a system becomes brittle doctrine rather than living governance.

nodes.label: Friction
nodes.description: Positive inheritance from the interaction with Dr. Brian: friction, path dependency, and systems thinking became design constraints for the research programme. Friction is not merely resistance but a diagnostic signal of structural misalignment.

nodes.label: Path Dependency
nodes.description: The constraint that past decisions limit future possibilities. Inherited from the interaction with Dr. Brian as a positive design constraint: the programme deliberately avoids tautological justification and post-hoc reasoning by acknowledging path dependency.

nodes.label: Evidence
nodes.description: Observable data that supports or undermines a proposition. A core component of Source of Justification, Constitutional Governance, and the Constitutional Reasoning Engine.

nodes.label: Reasoning
nodes.description: The logical process by which conclusions are derived from premises. Governed by the Sovereign Constitution and the Constitutional Reasoning Engine. Must be transparent, traceable, and revisable.

nodes.label: Responsibility
nodes.description: Explicit allocation of accountability for decisions and their consequences. A function of Constitutional Governance and the Sovereign Constitution (S7: Responsibility of Design).

nodes.label: Transparency (Governance)
nodes.description: Legibility of governance structures to their actors. Distinct from structural transparency: this is the transparency of reasoning logs, evidence trails, and decision accountability within constitutional governance.

nodes.label: Tautological Justification
nodes.description: An anti-pattern deliberately rejected by the research programme: using circular reasoning where the conclusion is embedded in the premise. Inherited negatively from the interaction with Dr. Brian.

nodes.label: Unfalsifiable Explanations
nodes.description: An anti-pattern deliberately rejected: explanations that cannot be tested against evidence. The programme requires every proposition to have falsification criteria.

nodes.label: Post-Hoc Reasoning
nodes.description: An anti-pattern deliberately rejected: constructing explanations after the fact to justify outcomes. The programme requires reasoning to precede and govern action, not follow it.

nodes.label: Emerging Research Programme
nodes.description: The unifying research question: What enduring structures consistently produce trustworthy, adaptive, and resilient systems? Domains differ (organizations, AI, governance, strategy, ethics) but the underlying question remains the same.

nodes.label: Dr. Brian Interaction
nodes.description: The constructive inheritance from the interaction with Dr. Brian: positive inheritance (friction, path dependency, systems thinking) became design constraints; negative inheritance (tautological justification, unfalsifiable explanations, post-hoc reasoning) became anti-patterns to reject.

nodes.label: AI Constitution ↔ LLM Reasoning
nodes.description: Example of the Stable/Adaptive Duality: the AI Constitution is the stable governance layer; LLM reasoning is the adaptive execution layer.

nodes.label: Architecture ↔ Features
nodes.description: Example of the Stable/Adaptive Duality: architecture is stable; features are adaptive.

nodes.label: Buddhism
nodes.description: A source of inspiration for the research programme. Generates hypotheses but does not validate them.

nodes.label: Business Experience
nodes.description: A source of inspiration for the research programme. Generates hypotheses but does not validate them.

nodes.label: Competing Explanations
nodes.description: Alternative hypotheses stored within each node of the Constitutional Reasoning Engine. Prevents single-narrative blindness.

nodes.label: Confidence
nodes.description: The degree of certainty attached to a proposition within the Constitutional Reasoning Engine. Subject to revision as evidence accumulates.

nodes.label: Constitution ↔ Legislation
nodes.description: Example of the Stable/Adaptive Duality: the constitution is stable; legislation is adaptive.

nodes.label: Daoism
nodes.description: A source of inspiration for the research programme. Generates hypotheses but does not validate them.

nodes.label: DNA ↔ Gene Expression
nodes.description: Example of the Stable/Adaptive Duality: DNA is stable; gene expression is adaptive.

nodes.label: Enduring Structures
nodes.description: The primary unit of study in Go-Shape Theory: structures that persist across time and generate recurring outcome patterns. The research programme asks what enduring structures consistently produce trustworthy, adaptive, and resilient systems.

nodes.label: Explainable AI
nodes.description: AI systems whose reasoning processes are legible, traceable, and accountable to human auditors. The Constitutional Reasoning Engine is a form of explainable AI.

nodes.label: Hypothesis
nodes.description: A testable proposition generated by sources of inspiration and validated by sources of justification. The central unit of the research methodology.

nodes.label: Knowledge Graph
nodes.description: The structured representation of the research programme's concepts, relationships, and evidence. Functions as the Constitutional Reasoning Engine when enriched with evidence, confidence, and amendment history.

nodes.label: Logical Consistency
nodes.description: The requirement that propositions within the research programme do not contradict each other. A component of Source of Justification.

nodes.label: Mission ↔ Strategy
nodes.description: Example of the Stable/Adaptive Duality: mission is stable; strategy is adaptive.

nodes.label: Predictive Power
nodes.description: The ability of a proposition to generate accurate predictions about future observations. A core criterion of Source of Justification.

nodes.label: Reasoning Links
nodes.description: Traceable connections between premises and conclusions within the Constitutional Reasoning Engine. Enable audit and revision of inference chains.

nodes.label: Systems Thinking
nodes.description: A source of inspiration and positive inheritance from the interaction with Dr. Brian. Generates holistic hypotheses about structural interactions.
